# Mera.jl

> Analysis of astrophysical simulation output in Julia. Reads RAMSES adaptive-mesh-refinement
> data natively (hydro and MHD, particles, gravity, clumps, sinks, radiative transfer), holds a
> snapshot as one table with one row per cell, and computes derived physics, regions, projections,
> profiles, phase diagrams and structure catalogues from it. Documentation:
> https://manuelbehrendt.github.io/Mera.jl/dev/

This file is a compact grounding for an AI assistant. It is not a tutorial. It states the data
model, the vocabulary, the mistakes that are easy to make, and how to check that an answer is
right. Everything below was verified against Mera 1.8, the development line until it is registered
(the last registered version is 1.7.0, which has none of the region values, `filterdata` or the
off-axis features named here).

## Data model

A snapshot is a table: one row per AMR cell, one column per quantity, and every row carries its
refinement `:level`. Nothing is resampled onto a uniform grid unless you ask with `covering_grid`.
Particles, clumps and sinks are separate objects with the same shape of interface.

Selections return **objects of the same type**, so calls chain: `subregion` into `filterdata`, and
the result goes to `getvar`, `msum`, `profile` or `projection`.

## Loading

    info = getinfo(400, "/path/to/sim")        # a RAMSES output folder
    gas  = gethydro(info; lmax=10)             # also getparticles/getgravity/getrt/getclumps/getsinks

    (; hydro, particles, info) = loadall(path, 400; components=[:hydro, :particles])

`loadall` dispatches on what it finds: a folder of RAMSES files goes through the RAMSES readers, a
folder holding `output_NNNNN.jld2` through `loaddata`. Prefer it when the code should work on both.
`getinfo` is RAMSES-only and **fails on a MERA-file folder**; `infodata` is its counterpart there.

Limit the read rather than trimming afterwards. Every getter, and `loadall`, takes
`xrange`/`yrange`/`zrange` with `center` and `range_unit`, and applies them while reading. The
defaults are the box corner and code units, so pass `center=[:bc], range_unit=:kpc`.

## Units: always say the unit

Every quantity takes a unit symbol, and the unit is part of the question:

    getvar(gas, :T, :K)
    msum(gas, :Msol)
    projection(gas, :sd, :Msol_pc2)
    filterdata(gas, Above(:T, 1e4, unit=:K))

`getvar(obj, :q)` without a unit returns **code units**, which mean something different in the next
simulation. `getvar()` with no arguments prints every derived quantity; `list_units()` prints the
units; `viewfields(obj)` shows what an object holds.

## Regions are values

    sphere(r; center=[:bc], range_unit=:kpc)        # centre is ABSOLUTE, in range_unit
    cuboid(xrange=[a,b], yrange=[c,d], zrange=[e,f], center=[:bc], range_unit=:kpc)
    cylinder(radius, half_height; axis=[0,0,1], center=[:bc], range_unit=:kpc)

Combine them with `∩` `∪` `\` `!`, meaning intersection, union, difference and complement, then
`subregion(obj, region)`. Every one has an ASCII spelling, so Unicode is never required:
`A & B`, `A | B`, `intersect(A, B)`, `union(A, B)`, `setdiff(A, B)`, `!A`. A ring is one
cylinder minus another. `subregion` splits boundary cells by default (`split=true`): a half-inside
cell keeps half of itself as `:fraction`, and that weighting carries through `getvar`, `msum` and
`projection`. Pass `split=false` for the classic whole-cell test. Only the value form splits: the
older `subregion(gas, :sphere, radius=...)` form keeps every intersecting cell whole and gives no
`:fraction`.

Two separate things, and they are easy to confuse:

- **`:fraction` makes the numbers exact.** It is on by default and needs no thought. A region and
  its complement add up to the parent.
- **`refine` / `refine_to` make the picture sharp.** `subregion(obj, region, refine_to=[0.05, :kpc])`
  subdivides each straddling cell until its children are no larger than the given length; match it
  to a projection's `pxsize` and the rendered boundary becomes pixel-sharp. It changes no total.

Points (particles, clumps, sinks) have no volume. Their in/out test is already exact, so leave
`split` out: `split=true` raises an error on particles, and clumps and sinks do not take it.

## Selecting by value

    hot   = filterdata(gas, Above(:T, 1e4, unit=:K))
    mask  = getmask(gas, Above(:T, 1e4, unit=:K))              # BitVector, pass as mask=
    band  = filterdata(gas, Above(:T, 1e4, unit=:K) & Below(:rho, 1e3, unit=:nH))

Predicates: `Above`, `Below`, `InRange`, `Equals`, `IsFinite`, `AbovePercentile`, `BelowPercentile`,
`Satisfies`, composed with `&` `|` `!`. They work on anything `getvar` computes, including derived
physics. `getmask(gas, region)` tests cell centres only, so `msum(gas, mask=getmask(gas, reg))` is
not the exact `msum(subregion(gas, reg))`.

## Computing

    projection(gas, :sd, :Msol_pc2; pxsize=[50.0, :pc], center=[:bc])
    projection(gas, :vlos, :km_s; center=[:bc], inclination=60.0, azimuth=30.0,
               fov=14.0, fov_unit=:kpc, aperture=:circle, split=true)
    profile(gas, :r_cylinder, :T; xunit=:kpc, unit=:K)     # also profile3d, profiletimeseries
    phase(gas, :rho, :T; xunit=:nH, yunit=:K)
    velocitydispersion(gas; center=[:bc])                   # a radial sigma profile
    clumpfind(gas, :rho; threshold=1e2, threshold_unit=:nH, linking_length=0.2)   # 7 finders
    timeseries(...)                                         # one snapshot in memory at a time

Use `pxsize=[value, :unit]` rather than `res=`. `:sd`, `:vlos` and `:σlos` are not in `getvar`:
they need a camera, so they exist in `projection` (and `:vlos` in `volumerender`).

Single numbers: `msum`, `center_of_mass`, `bulk_velocity`, `getextent`,
`wstat` (mean, median, std, skewness, kurtosis, extrema, optionally weighted and masked).

## Traps

These are mistakes an assistant makes confidently. Each was reproduced.

1. **`@filter` compares in code units.** `@filter gas :T > 1e4` is not ten thousand Kelvin. On one
   test run `1e4` code units is `6.8e9` K, so it selected 0 cells while
   `Above(:T, 1e4, unit=:K)` selected all 849332. The macro is fine for `:level` or for a
   threshold you already have in code units; for physics, name the unit with `Above`/`Below`.
   The macro also takes one comparison only; `&` `|` `!` need the predicate form.
2. **The region constructors are lowercase.** `sphere`, `cylinder`, `cuboid`,
   `sphericalshell`, `cylindricalshell`. Capitalized `Sphere`/`Cylinder` are not exported,
   because Makie exports those names too and a name exported by two loaded packages binds to
   neither. The types are still reachable as `Mera.Sphere` for dispatch.
3. **`projection` does honour cell fractions.** It reaches mass through `getvar`, so a map of a
   split subregion totals exactly what `msum` reports (with `fov`, only when `split=true`).
4. **`extent` is absolute, `cextent` is measured from `center`.** `cextent` is symmetric only when
   the centre sits in the middle of the window. Plot with `cextent` when the axis is centred.
5. **`fov` fixes the frame; `aperture=:square` then crops it.** The frame is ±`fov` about `center`
   at every angle, also for sparse data such as a star disc. The square keeps only what lies
   inside it, so never read a total off a `:square` map. For a total, use `aperture=:circle`
   together with `split=true`, or leave out `fov`. Projection's default is `split=false`, which keeps
   every cell the sphere touches whole (7 % too much mass in a 5 kpc aperture on Mera's test
   galaxy), while
   `subregion` defaults to `split=true`. `depth` cuts a slab along the view and also needs
   `split=true` to be exact; it is refused on axis-aligned calls, where `zrange` does the job.
6. **`@where` and `@apply` act on the raw table** (`gas.data`), not on the Mera object.
7. **On particles, `:mass` is a mean and the face-on axis includes the dark matter.** A particle
   has no volume, so `projection(part, :mass)` is the mass-weighted mean particle mass per pixel;
   use `mode=:sum`, or `:sd` times the pixel area, for a total. `direction=:faceon` and
   `axis=:angmom` sum over every particle drawn, so the halo usually sets the axis: pass
   `parttypes=[:stars]` or a mask, or compute `L = angmom(...)` and pass `axis=L`.
8. **`refine` does not improve accuracy.** It is tempting to reach for it to make a mass "more
   exact". The integrals were already exact through `:fraction`, and a straddling cell's children
   inherit its piecewise-constant values, so their fraction-weighted volumes telescope back to the
   parent's. Refining changes what a boundary looks like, not what it weighs.
9. **Radii and velocities need a frame.** `getvar`, `filterdata`, the getters and `projection`
   measure from the box corner unless you pass `center` (`center=[:bc]` for the box centre).
   Region constructors and `profile` default to `[:bc]`, so a region and a getter given the same
   numbers can mean different places. Velocity quantities such as `:mach` or `:vϕ_cylinder` are in
   the box frame unless you pass `vcenter`.
10. **Distances are not periodic unless you ask.** Use `:r_sphere_periodic` or
   `:r_cylinder_periodic`, and `center_of_mass(...; periodic=true)`. `getinfo` reports what the
   namelist implies as `info.boundaries`, and Mera never acts on it by itself.
11. **`getvar(grav, :epot)` is corrected, the raw column is not.** RAMSES stores the potential short
   by a factor `boxlen`; `getvar` multiplies it back. The raw column `grav.data.epot`, and so
   `@where`/`@apply` on it, holds RAMSES's uncorrected value.

## Write it so a person can read it

Analysis code is read far more often than it is written, usually by someone deciding whether to
trust the number. Code produced for a Mera user should look like the examples above:

- **Short and flat.** Prefer a few named steps to one dense expression. `subregion` then
  `filterdata` then `projection` reads as a sentence; the same thing nested does not.
- **Name the physical constants.** `R_DISC = 14.0  # kpc, disc radius` rather than a bare `14.0`
  four lines down. A reader should be able to change the science without hunting.
- **Comment the decisions, not the syntax.** Nobody needs `# project the gas`. They do need to know
  why the colour range is fixed, why the aperture is circular, why that temperature cut.
- **Say the unit in the code**, not only in a comment, by using the unit arguments.
- **Leave the check in.** The partition check below is three lines and belongs in the script, not
  in a throwaway REPL session.

## Checking the answer

An assistant should not hand back a number without one of these. They are cheap.

**Code.** A condition and its negation must reproduce the parent, for regions and for values alike:

    a = msum(subregion(gas, reg), :Msol)
    b = msum(subregion(gas, !reg), :Msol)
    abs(a + b - msum(gas, :Msol)) / msum(gas, :Msol)     # measured 0.0

Same for `filterdata(gas, cond)` against `filterdata(gas, !cond)`. This catches an inverted
comparison, a wrong unit and a mis-specified region in one line. A projected map should also total
its `msum` when it has no `fov`, or when `fov` is used with `split=true`.

**Physics.** Prefer a case with a known answer. `download_testdata()` fetches fifteen public test
simulations, about 300 MB together (or one by name, `download_testdata("sedov3d_amr")`), chosen for
exactly this: a Sedov blast whose radius grows as `t^(2/5)`, an MHD
shock tube where a divergence-free field keeps `Bx` constant, four density blobs that a clump
finder must return as four, a Strömgren sphere whose ionisation front follows the analytic law, and
three of RAMSES's own tests checked against published reference values. Beyond that: check limiting
cases, check a total against an independent route, and check that a result does not move when the
pixel size, the viewing angle or the thread count changes.

**Reproducibility.** Record what produced a number:

    provenance_string(gas)    # version, git branch and commit, dirty flag, snapshot, time
    mera_build()              # distinguishes a registry install from a checkout of a branch

`pkgversion` reports the same string for a release and for a development checkout, so a result from
a branch looks like a result from the release unless `mera_build` is used. Saved maps and reports
carry provenance with them. For a shared analysis, pin the environment in a `Project.toml` next to
the script and commit the `Manifest.toml` that `instantiate` produces.

## Also in Mera

- `volumerender(gas, :rho, ...)` with `volumelook`, `volumeorbit` and `volumepath` renders hydro
  data as a translucent volume. Orthographic only, no perspective fly-through.
- `repartition(output, path, ncpu)` rewrites a RAMSES output for another number of CPUs,
  `writeramses(ncpu; hydro, gravity, particles, ...)` writes one from Mera data or a mera file,
  `compareramses` checks two outputs, and `restart_completeness(gas; ...)` says what a restart
  still lacks.
- `face_on`, `edge_on` and `angmom` give a frame to pass to `projection`; `periodic_recenter(map;
  center)` moves a finished map across a periodic box so a structure on a face appears whole.

**Not part of Mera:** emission or extinction transfer functions, `column_integral`, line-of-sight
cubes, kinematic mock observations and their FITS export, a fly-through renderer, and a
`rotationcurve` function. Do not write code that calls them.
